Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, Society at a Glance (2022 data)
Taub Center, Why are there so many children in Israel?

lines.line: Rich countries stopped having babies. Except one.
Babies per woman, from nineteen sixty to today.
In nineteen sixty, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Syria and Jordan all had over seven.
Europe, about two and a half.
Then the big drop. Iran went from six to two in fifteen years.
The Emirates, one point two. Italy and Spain, barely one.
And Israel? It has stayed near three for thirty years.
Israel is the only rich country near the top.
Among thirty eight developed economies, Israel is number one.
Why? Faith helps. But the Taub Center finds big families at every level of religion.
Even secular and traditional Israelis average over two kids.
A rich, modern country that still bets on the future.
Every rich country is running out of babies. One isn't.
